topic: How does non-optimal switching threshold selection impact end-to-end link KPIs like outage probability and latency?
consensus_response: Non-optimal switching threshold selection significantly impacts end-to-end link KPIs, particularly outage probability and latency. It compromises the benefits of adaptive modulation schemes in multi-beam systems, leading to reduced effective bandwidth (Beff) and capacity blocking. Increased spatial correlation between gws results from non-optimal switching, compromising beamforming benefits and increasing interference. This interaction exacerbates latency due to increased packet loss and retransmissions, degrading overall system performance.
reference_context: Non-optimal switching threshold selection affects the trade-off between outage probability and latency in multi-beam systems by compromising adaptive modulation schemes and beamforming benefits.
